unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U13: Distinguish retirement,expulsion and insolvency effects

payload.title: Record both internal exit and external liability
payload.core_explanation_md:
Retirement may follow consent, an express agreement or the described at-will written-notice route. An internal exit date does not alone settle a third party claim. Public notice and the specified exceptions matter for later acts; release from existing obligations needs the applicable creditor agreement rather than a private promise between partners.

Expulsion requires a contractual power exercised in good faith; a bare majority is not a universal expulsion power. Insolvency has its own statutory cessation point at the adjudication order and rules for subsequent firm/estate liability. Keep retirement, expulsion, death and insolvency as distinct events rather than recording all of them simply as account-signatory changes.

self_check.prompt_text: Does removing a bank signatory automatically release earlier firm debt?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Existing liability and creditor discharge require separate analysis.

options.text_md: The existing-debt liability and any creditor release must be examined separately
options.explanation_md: Internal retirement does not automatically erase earlier obligations.

options.explanation_md: The source does not support that result.

payload.stem_md: A majority expels a partner without checking the agreement or good faith. Which requirement was missed?

options.explanation_md: Balance does not create expulsion power.

options.text_md: A universal right of any majority to expel
The expelled person consent to every ordinary purchase
options.explanation_md: Consent for ordinary purchasing does not establish a contractual power of expulsion exercised in good faith.

options.text_md: A contractual expulsion power exercised in good faith
options.explanation_md: Both elements matter in the described framework.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Both elements matter in the described framework.
